title: POSIX sh (launcher, git hook, eval scaffolds)

versions.version: POSIX sh, researched against POSIX.1-2024 (Issue 8); must also run on dash (Linux), bash 3.2 / zsh as sh (macOS) and Git Bash (MSYS2) sh on Windows
versions.pinnedIn: not pinned: #!/bin/sh in plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh, .githooks/pre-commit, fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh; hooks.json invokes `sh` explicitly

rules.rule: In a #!/bin/sh file use only POSIX features: no [[ ]], ==, local, source, $'...', arrays, function keyword, echo -e/-n. A script that needs bash says #!/bin/bash (as the eval scaffolds do) and is run with bash.
rules.why: The same file runs under dash, macOS sh and Git Bash; a bashism works on the author's shell and fails (syntax error or wrong branch) on another, and in the guard hook that means the hook errors on one OS only.

rules.rule: Do not rely on `set -o pipefail` in a #!/bin/sh file, and do not put a command whose failure matters on the left of a pipe. Check it separately (write to a temp file, or run it first) or move the script to bash.
rules.why: Without pipefail a pipeline's status is its last command's, so set -e does not stop on a failed left side. pipefail is POSIX only since 1003.1-2024 and dash gained it only in 0.5.13; older dash ignores or rejects it. In copy_tree, a failing `cd` or `find` left of `| while read` is invisible: the scaffold continues and commits an incomplete fixture.
where: fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh copy_tree: `(cd "$1" && find ...) | while IFS= read -r f`

rules.rule: Double-quote every parameter expansion and command substitution ("$cli", "$@", "$(dirname -- "$0")"). To run a command held in variables, pass it as function arguments and expand "$@" (the launcher's `ok py -3` pattern), not as an unquoted string.
rules.why: Unquoted expansions are field-split on IFS and glob-expanded. The plugin root and repo live under paths with spaces and non-ASCII characters (the dev home is Cyrillic); one unquoted path splits into several arguments and the launcher runs the wrong file or none.
rules.repoConvention: .githooks/pre-commit deliberately leaves `$py` unquoted so the value `py -3` splits into command + argument (pick_python echoes it). Safe only because pick_python returns one of three fixed strings; ShellCheck reports it as SC2086. Follow the repo, never extend the pattern to values that contain paths.

rules.rule: Follow every `cd` with `|| exit 1` (or `|| return` in a function), or use it as an `&&`/`if` condition.
rules.why: A failed cd leaves the script in the old directory and the next commands (git add -A, cp, rm) act on the wrong tree; ShellCheck flags a bare cd as SC2164.

rules.rule: Resolve a script's own directory with `CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd` inside $( ), keeping the empty CDPATH prefix and the `--`.
rules.why: When cd resolves through a non-empty CDPATH it writes the new path to stdout, so the captured value becomes two lines and every path built from it is wrong. `--` stops a path that starts with `-` being read as an option. The `VAR= cmd` form matches ShellCheck SC1007's pattern; here the empty environment value is the intent (CDPATH='' is the explicit equivalent).

rules.rule: Probe an interpreter by running the version check itself, as `ok()` does; use `command -v`, never `which`, when only presence matters. Keep `2>/dev/null` on probes.
rules.why: A name found on PATH is not a usable interpreter: on Windows `python`/`python3` can be Store/install-manager aliases that open the Store or install a runtime, and on any OS the found Python may be older than 3.11. `command -v` is the POSIX presence test (no output, non-zero status when not found); `which` is not specified.

rules.rule: End the launcher with `exec` of the real command and treat its exit status as the hook verdict: 0 lets the call proceed (JSON decides), 2 blocks it, anything else is a non-blocking failure. A shell path of the launcher must never exit 2, and `guard` with no usable Python must keep exiting 0.
rules.why: exec replaces the shell, so Python's exit status reaches Claude Code unchanged; a stray exit 2 (from the shell or the CLI) blocks the user's tool call. Fail-open for a missing Python is a stated design (hooks.json description).

rules.rule: Keep `onFailure: continue` on the guard hook and keep the command in shell form `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stackfoundry.sh" guard` with the placeholder inside double quotes.
rules.why: On Windows hooks run in Git Bash, or in PowerShell when Git Bash is missing; there `sh` cannot start, and without Git Bash any exit other than 0 or 2 from a PreToolUse hook counts as a failure. onFailure decides whether that failure blocks every Edit/Bash call. Unquoted, a plugin root with spaces splits.

rules.rule: Under `set -u`, read optional positional parameters as `${1:-}` / `${2:-}`.
rules.why: Expanding an unset parameter under set -u is an error that aborts a non-interactive shell, so calling `scaffold <fixture>` without the second argument would fail.

rules.rule: Do not rely on set -e inside functions or on `A && B || C` as if-then-else; write explicit `|| { msg; exit 1; }` or an if block.
rules.why: set -e is ignored for every command of an AND-OR list but the last and in if/while conditions, including inside functions called from there, so a failure is silently skipped. With `A && B || C`, C also runs when B fails (SC2015).

rules.rule: Print data (paths, user input) with `printf '%s\n' "$x"`, not echo.
rules.why: POSIX states echo cannot be used portably unless escape sequences are omitted and the first argument does not start with - followed by e, E or n, and encourages printf for new applications; a path containing backslashes (Windows paths) or starting with -n/-e may print differently across shells.
where: not used here yet (current echo calls print fixed text or fixed command names)

rules.rule: Keep shell files LF: .gitattributes pins `*.sh`, `.githooks/*` and `plugins/stackfoundry/bin/*` to eol=lf; a new shell file outside these patterns gets its own line, and after changing .gitattributes run `git add --renormalize .`.
rules.why: A CR in a script is read literally (`exit 1\r`, `then\r`), giving 'command not found' or syntax errors on every OS; core.autocrlf on Windows would otherwise convert on checkout. Changing attributes does not rewrite files already committed.

rules.rule: When a script on Windows passes paths to a native program (python.exe, py.exe), expect MSYS2 to rewrite POSIX-looking arguments; exclude arguments that only look like paths with MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL, or convert explicitly with cygpath.
rules.why: The launcher's `exec python -I "$cli"` relies on this conversion to hand python.exe a Windows path; an argument such as `/foo` or `a:/b` that is not a path gets rewritten and the CLI sees a wrong value.

rules.rule: When a script parses path lists from git (ls-files, diff --name-only), use -z or `-c core.quotePath=false`.
rules.why: By default git C-quotes paths with bytes over 0x80, so a Cyrillic file name arrives as "\320\220..." and no longer matches the file on disk.

bugCategories.name: unquoted-path-expansion
bugCategories.lookFor: $var, $(cmd) or $@ outside double quotes in a command argument, test or assignment used later as an argument.
bugCategories.failure: A path with spaces or glob characters splits into several arguments; the launcher or scaffold acts on a wrong or missing file.

bugCategories.name: bashism-in-sh
bugCategories.lookFor: [[ ]], ==, local, source, arrays, $'...', echo -e, set -o pipefail in a file with #!/bin/sh or run as `sh file`.
bugCategories.failure: Syntax error or wrong branch under dash or older shells while passing on the author's bash.

bugCategories.name: masked-pipeline-failure
bugCategories.lookFor: A command whose failure matters on the left of `|` in a sh script, relying on set -e.
bugCategories.failure: The script continues after the left side failed and produces partial output (e.g. a fixture committed with files missing).

bugCategories.name: unchecked-cd
bugCategories.lookFor: `cd` not followed by `|| exit`/`|| return` nor used as a condition; `cd` inside $( ) without CDPATH=.
bugCategories.failure: Later commands run in the wrong directory, or a captured directory contains an extra line from CDPATH output.

bugCategories.name: hook-exit-misverdict
bugCategories.lookFor: Any path through scripts/stackfoundry.sh that can exit 2, or exit non-zero for `guard` when Python is missing; edits removing `exec` or onFailure.
bugCategories.failure: Every Edit/Bash tool call is blocked (exit 2 or onFailure block) or the guard silently stops guarding.

bugCategories.name: interpreter-probe-false-positive
bugCategories.lookFor: Choosing python by `command -v` or `which` alone, without running a version check.
bugCategories.failure: The script picks a Store alias or an old Python and fails or opens the Store instead of falling through to the next candidate.

bugCategories.name: crlf-script
bugCategories.lookFor: A new shell file outside the .gitattributes eol=lf patterns, or `\r` in a script (`cat -v` shows ^M).
bugCategories.failure: 'command not found' / syntax errors from literal CRs, typically only on clones made on Windows.

bugCategories.name: msys-arg-mangling
bugCategories.lookFor: Arguments to native Windows programs that begin with / or contain : and are not paths.
bugCategories.failure: MSYS2 rewrites the argument to a Windows path; the program receives a wrong value on Windows only.

bugCategories.name: quoted-git-paths
bugCategories.lookFor: Parsing newline-separated git path output without -z or core.quotePath=false.
bugCategories.failure: Non-ASCII file names arrive octal-escaped in double quotes and are skipped or treated as missing.

testing.layers: Shell behaviour is proved end to end from Python unittest by running the real script under `sh` in a temp repo; the launcher's Python selection and fail-open path have no direct test yet.
traps: Both shell tests are skipUnless(shutil.which("sh")): on a machine or runner where sh is not on PATH they skip silently and CI stays green; check the skip count on the Windows job.

No test runs the launcher with no usable Python (guard must exit 0, other subcommands 127) or from a directory whose path contains spaces or non-ASCII characters; add them by running the launcher with a PATH stripped of Python and from a temp dir named with a space and Cyrillic letters.
ShellCheck is not run anywhere (no config, no CI step). Recommended: `shellcheck -s sh` on the #!/bin/sh files and `-s bash` on the eval scaffolds; flag for /stackfoundry:scaffold-test-harness.

security.note: The launcher runs Python with -I so a module planted in the user's repo is not imported; keep -I on every exec branch. Source files with `.` only by a path containing a slash (as the scaffolds build from $0): a bare name is searched on PATH.

performance.note: The guard runs before every Edit/Write/Bash call with a 10 s timeout and each probe starts a Python process; a timed-out PreToolUse hook does not block, so a slow probe chain silently disables the guard. Keep the fastest likely candidate first and add no extra probes.

pins: None: shebangs #!/bin/sh (launcher, pre-commit, scaffold-lib) and #!/bin/bash (eval scaffolds).
lockStep: the Python floor 3.11 in scripts/stackfoundry.sh ok() and .githooks/pre-commit pick_python must stay equal
deprecationsInUse: `py -3` (scripts/stackfoundry.sh, .githooks/pre-commit): the -3 short form belongs to the legacy py launcher, deprecated since Python 3.14 in favour of the Python install manager, which accepts tags starting with 3 without `V:` for compatibility.

notReached: Bash manual for the eval scaffolds (#!/bin/bash, set -euo pipefail): not researched; the scaffolds only source scaffold-lib.sh, which is covered as POSIX sh.
Apple documentation on macOS /bin/sh (bash 3.2 / zsh in sh mode): not read; macOS behaviour rests on the POSIX rules and CI's macos job.
Official Claude Code docs on the path format of CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT on Windows: the hooks page does not state it; only issue-tracker reports (backslash stripping, closed early 2026) were found.
questions: .githooks/pre-commit runs `$py -m unittest` unquoted so `py -3` splits (SC2086); scripts/stackfoundry.sh uses the POSIX alternative of passing the command as function arguments. Keep the hook as is, or align it with the launcher?
fixtures/scaffold-lib.sh copy_tree pipes `(cd "$1" && find ...)` into `while read` under set -e without pipefail: a failure on the left is masked. Accept (fixtures are controlled) or restructure?

With the Python install manager on Windows and no runtime installed, a launch command may try to install a runtime; whether `py -3` / the `python` alias does so inside the 10 s guard timeout is not documented. Worth a Windows check of the launcher's probe chain?
Add a ShellCheck step to CI (no config exists today)?
